sourceReview.locator: syllabus/Stage 3 Content.md:274-288 — Whole numbers: Recognise, represent and order numbers in the millions
sourceReview.observation: Directly supports naming millions through the place value grouping of ones, tens and hundreds. The existing theory correctly explains three-digit periods, place names, zero placeholders and digit value: the $7$ in $4\,728\,000$ represents $700\,000$. Its writing convention supports reading numerals accurately. Ordering and rounding belong to sibling skills; the two rounding examples do not establish an additional method for this skill. Retain Stage 3 scope and the existing theory.

sourceReview.locator: booklets/mathsmap-sources/Stage 4/Fractions Decimals Percentages 3_Converting FDP.md:956-1023 — Converting Fractions and Decimals; Review; Decimals to Fractions using Decimal Place; Convert decimals to fractions
sourceReview.observation: The complete supplied section reviews decimal–fraction conversion and teaches writing a decimal as a fraction using decimal places, then simplifying. Its worked conversions and practice reinforce positional value, but do not teach naming whole numbers in the millions. They supply no additional assessed method or suitable worked example for this skill. Decimal conversion, powers-of-ten denominators and fraction simplification remain outside this Stage 3 assignment.

sourceReview.path: booklets/mathsmap-sources/Stage 5 Core/Numbers of Any Magnitude 2_Find absolute and percentage error.md
sourceReview.observation: The teaching explicitly identifies precision and then halves it to obtain absolute error. The source examples show $18$ kg giving precision $1$ kg and absolute error $0.5$ kg, and $18.4$ kg giving precision $0.1$ kg and absolute error $0.05$ kg. Practice includes an explicit nearest-$10$ mL instruction, supporting precedence over the displayed units place. The Key Idea concerns the subsequent percentage-error calculation, which belongs to the dependent skill. These examples and practice support one precision-and-halving method for the assigned Stage 5 skill.
adjustments: Qualify the place-value rule so explicitly stated accuracy takes precedence.
Clarify that half the precision represents maximum possible rounding error.
Retain the source examples and practice values; no numerical changes are required.

sourceReview.path: booklets/mathsmap-sources/Stage 5 Core/Numbers of Any Magnitude 2_Find absolute and percentage error.md
sourceReview.locator: Percentage Error — complete first practice question
sourceReview.observation: All four parts are consistent: the $251$ g measurement has precision $1$ g, absolute error $0.5$ g, bounds $250.5$ g and $251.5$ g, and percentage error $0.20\%$ to two decimal places. The limits support the existing supplementary bounds content. The source states the endpoints as a range without specifying endpoint inclusion; the theory's explicit inequality needs the usual positive half-up rounding convention stated. No original figure is declared in this section.
adjustments: Preserve all source parts, values, units and the stated two-decimal-place percentage answer.
Correct the theory's upper-endpoint inclusion under the explicitly stated rounding convention.
Retain the existing theory diagram without claiming visual acceptance.
